transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening about 1 week after your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

However, if you don't have any yet and need some, I'd recommend getting preservative-free eye drops from your pharmacist. You can use them four times daily to start, especially if you're experiencing any dryness, grittiness, or watery eyes.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I do have another one. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. 

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one last question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, and this should improve quickly over time.

However, I don't have your specific details, so I'm not sure exactly how long it's been since your operation. If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I had. Thank you for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm, have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thanks again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best wishes with your recovery.
